included: the two-way roster-to-statement match
per-client movement explained by a named mechanism
dated discrepancy cases with the partner contact
tracking program-term changes
the verify-current-terms discipline
excluded: asserting any rate, percentage, per-client amount or tier threshold
the acquisition-stage evaluation of a partner program including attribution and clawback windows
the client own invoice from the platform, which is between them
the tax treatment of the operator own revenue

pros.claim: A two-way match catches revenue that quietly stopped, which no total-level glance will ever reveal
pros.example: a client still being served whose credit disappeared after a platform account change nobody flagged

pros.claim: Understanding the movement mechanisms turns a residual into a forecastable line rather than a surprise
pros.example: knowing that a seasonal headcount swing moves the amount because the program carries a per-employee element

cons.claim: The operator has limited visibility and limited leverage because the counterparty owns both the ledger and the terms
cons.example: a statement format that does not show the driver behind a per-client change

cons.claim: Reconciliation is administrative work with no client-facing value and it is easy to skip while the total looks roughly right
cons.example: three periods passing before anyone notices a missing client credit

failure_modes: checking only the total
assuming an unfamiliar client on the statement belongs to you
missing a program term change
letting a difference age past the partner own inquiry window
planning on last year terms
acceptance_tests: every statement period has a recorded two-way match against the served roster, with each difference either explained by a named mechanism or opened as a dated case with the partner contact
revisit_triggers: the partner program changes terms, tiers, crediting rules or statement format
a client plan, headcount or discount status changes
a gap appears between the roster and the statement
the operator crosses a book-size boundary the program tiering uses

base.update_signal: a partner-program term or statement change, or a per-client movement that no known mechanism explains

nodes.definition: A payroll book does not scale by client count; it scales by the shape of the work, and the binding constraint is that the work is synchronized. Most small employers pay on the same few dates, quarter close lands on everybody at once and year-end lands on everybody at once, so a book sized against average workload fails precisely on the days that matter. The unit is segmentation plus a capacity model built from mechanisms: clients grouped by complexity class covering jurisdictions, pay types, benefits, orders and entity count, by service tier covering approval-only against full data entry, and by run day; peak-day load computed from the clients who actually cluster on the same date rather than from a monthly average; quarter-close and year-end season loads estimated separately because those are the real failure points; and a stated reserve for the incident and correction work that arrives unscheduled by definition. Out of that model come real decisions: which pay date a new client is placed on, which complexity classes the practice will accept at all, when the next hire or the next standardization step has to happen, and the decision operators avoid, which clients are structurally unprofitable or unservable at the current quality bar and should be repriced or referred elsewhere. Capacity here is always a mechanism the operator recomputes from their own time records, never a client-count figure borrowed from another practice.

included: segmentation by complexity, service tier and run day
peak-day and season load modelling from the operator own recorded time
a reserve for unscheduled correction work
placement, acceptance, hiring and repricing decisions
excluded: any borrowed or published clients-per-person figure
pricing methodology for new business
the onboarding project effort estimate
employment decisions about staff, which are the operator own business and legal matter

pros.claim: Peak-day modelling prevents the failure that actually happens, which is a cluster of runs on one date rather than a full month
pros.example: discovering that most of the book pays on the same two semi-monthly dates before adding another client to that cluster

pros.claim: An explicit unservable-client decision protects the run quality that all retention depends on
pros.example: referring out a multi-jurisdiction client whose complexity exceeds what the practice can carry at its current standard

cons.claim: The model requires the operator to track their own time honestly, which most practices do not do
cons.example: a capacity estimate built on remembered effort that understates correction work entirely

cons.claim: Segmentation can harden into neglect of the small clients who were the practice origin and its referral source
cons.example: an early client with one employee who introduced three others receiving the least attention

failure_modes: sizing the book by averages
adding a complex client without adding capacity
letting quarter and year-end seasons collide with a growth push
keeping a structurally unprofitable client out of loyalty until the whole book quality suffers
acceptance_tests: the capacity model is built from the operator own recorded time by complexity class, states peak-day and season loads separately, and carries a named reserve for unscheduled correction work
every new client is placed against the model before its pay date is agreed
revisit_triggers: a peak day is missed or a season slips
the book complexity mix shifts
staffing changes
an expansion service adds recurring load to existing days

base.update_signal: a missed peak-day or season commitment, which recalibrates the modelled load per complexity class

nodes.definition: The expansion advantage of a payroll relationship is not access to the owner; it is that the recurring work already produces evidence of what the client is missing, so the right offer can be made from observation rather than from a script. The discipline is to name the signals and where each one appears. Entries the client cannot explain, a bookkeeping function that is really the owner at midnight, or a client who cannot say what their payroll expense was last quarter, all point at bookkeeping. Onboarding paperwork arriving incomplete, no offer letters, no handbook, no record of policy acknowledgements, or a termination handled by text message, point at human-resources documentation and process. Repeated timecard disputes and manual timesheet transcription point at time and attendance. Benefit deductions that do not tie to a carrier invoice, or an owner asking what they could offer to keep staff, point at a benefits introduction subject to the licensing boundary. A workers-compensation audit surprise or a premium computed from estimated payroll points at a pay-as-you-go or broker introduction. Repeated late funding and no visibility of cash points at something the operator may not be the right provider for at all. Every signal is logged with its evidence and its date, and the offer is made when the need is live, usually right after the event that made it visible, rather than saved for a quarterly sales push. The honest half of this unit is the negative: some observed needs are not the operator to serve, and naming the need and referring it is worth more to the relationship than an ill-fitting add-on.

included: the signal catalogue and the evidence source for each
logging signal, evidence and date
timing the offer to the live need
the refer-out-instead-of-stretch rule
excluded: the ethics and disclosure rules governing the offer itself
the licensing boundary on benefits, retirement and insurance introductions
manufacturing a need the evidence does not support
the acquisition-stage discovery interview with a prospect

pros.claim: An evidence-based offer lands as service rather than as selling
pros.example: proposing bookkeeping in the week a client could not answer a simple question about last quarter payroll expense

pros.claim: Logging signals prevents the common pattern where the operator sees everything and acts on nothing
pros.example: three dated observations of incomplete new-hire paperwork becoming one specific documentation proposal

cons.claim: The operator sees more than the client agreed to be advised on, so unsolicited observations can read as judgement
cons.example: commenting on how a termination was handled when nobody asked

cons.claim: A signal is not a mandate, and some owners genuinely prefer the arrangement the signal flags
cons.example: an owner who does their own books deliberately and has no intention of stopping

failure_modes: turning observations into a pitch list
waiting for a quarterly review when the need was live in week two
offering a service the practice cannot deliver at the current quality bar
ignoring signals that point to a referral rather than to a sale
acceptance_tests: every logged need signal carries its evidence, its date and a recorded disposition of offered, referred out or deliberately not pursued, with the reason
revisit_triggers: the client business changes shape
a signal class recurs across the book, suggesting a standard service
the practice adds or drops a capability

base.update_signal: an expansion that succeeded or failed against the signal that prompted it, which re-weights the catalogue

nodes.definition: The services around payroll look like a natural ladder and each rung carries a different burden, so the honest question is not what can be added but what each addition demands of the practice. Bookkeeping is the closest neighbour and the heaviest: monthly recurring work with its own deadlines, its own software, its own reconciliation discipline, a professional-standards question about what unlicensed bookkeeping may and may not include, and a doubling of the practice exposure to the client year-end. Human-resources add-ons, such as handbook and policy documentation, onboarding paperwork, record retention and training tracking, sell easily off payroll signals but carry an advice boundary sharper than payroll own, because employment questions arrive constantly and the answers are jurisdiction-specific and legally consequential. Time and attendance is mostly configuration and support load and is the least professionally risky rung, but it makes the operator responsible for a system whose failures land on run day. Benefits, retirement plan and workers-compensation introductions are not service work at all in most arrangements; they are referrals into licensed channels with their own compensation disclosure and licensing obligation classes. Every rung is assessed against four questions before it is offered: what recurring load does it add and on which calendar days, what licensing or professional obligation class applies and must be verified in the operating jurisdiction, what happens to the payroll service quality if it goes wrong, and can the practice deliver it at the standard the payroll book already holds.

included: rung-by-rung assessment of recurring load, obligation class, quality risk and capability
the four evaluation questions
the interaction of each rung with existing peak days and seasons
excluded: the licensing and disclosure rules themselves beyond naming the class to verify
the selling conversation and its ethics
asserting margins, prices or attach rates for any service
performing regulated professional work in an adjacent field

pros.claim: Assessing a rung before selling it prevents the classic implosion where a new service degrades the payroll book that funded it
pros.example: seeing that monthly closes for several bookkeeping clients would land in the same week as quarter-end payroll work

pros.claim: Some rungs are genuinely low risk and high fit, and naming why lets the practice grow deliberately
pros.example: time tracking that removes a recurring cause of run-day defects rather than adding one

cons.claim: The assessment slows an expansion the client is asking for right now
cons.example: a client wanting bookkeeping to start next month while the load question is still open

cons.claim: Rungs interact badly: a human-resources add-on increases the volume of exactly the questions the advice boundary must send away
cons.example: a handbook engagement producing weekly employment-law questions the operator cannot answer

failure_modes: adding bookkeeping without capacity for its month-end
treating human-resources documents as low risk because they are templates
accepting a referral fee without checking the licensing class
adding a rung whose failure mode lands on the payroll service credibility
acceptance_tests: each offered rung has a written assessment of its recurring load by calendar day, the obligation class to verify, the failure impact on the payroll service and a capability decision
no rung is offered to a client before that assessment exists
revisit_triggers: a rung real load differs from its assessment
a licensing or professional-standards change
the platform adds or removes a module that changes a rung economics
the payroll defect trend moves after a rung is added

base.update_signal: a rung whose real load or obligation class differed materially from the pre-sale assessment

nodes.definition: The moment a payroll conversation turns to health benefits, a retirement plan, workers-compensation coverage or any insurance product, the operator has walked to the edge of a licensed profession, and the rules on the other side are not payroll rules. Three obligation classes govern the crossing and each is verified in the operating jurisdiction and with the receiving professional rather than assumed: who may be compensated for an insurance or securities-adjacent introduction and under what registration or licensing status, what may be said before a conversation becomes solicitation or advice, and what disclosure the referring party owes the client about how they are paid. The practical discipline follows from those. Describe the mechanism, such as how a pay-as-you-go arrangement computes premium from actual payroll each run instead of from an estimate, and never the recommendation that a particular plan or carrier is right for this client. Introduce a licensed professional and step out of the advice thread rather than translating between the parties. Disclose any compensation arrangement in writing before the introduction, plainly enough that the client understands the operator is not neutral, and record the client consent to the introduction. Retirement plans deserve their own caution, because the fiduciary and securities questions there are materially heavier than an ordinary product introduction and the payroll operator role is typically the data connection rather than anything resembling plan advice. None of this is about being unhelpful; a warm, well-briefed introduction genuinely serves the client. It is about the introduction being only that.

included: the three obligation classes to verify before any compensated introduction
the mechanism-not-recommendation speech rule
written compensation disclosure before the introduction and a recorded consent
stepping out of the advice thread
the heavier retirement-plan caution
excluded: stating who is licensed to do what in any jurisdiction or what any arrangement pays
benefits, insurance, investment or retirement advice of any kind
deciding a client coverage or plan
the referral-partner economics of the payroll program itself

pros.claim: A disclosed and consented introduction is durable and protects the payroll relationship underneath it
pros.example: the client learning about the compensation arrangement in writing from the operator rather than later from the broker

pros.claim: Staying out of the advice thread keeps the licensed professional accountable for their own advice
pros.example: declining to summarise plan options for the client and letting the adviser present them directly

cons.claim: Disclosure sometimes reduces the client enthusiasm for an introduction, which is a genuine commercial cost of doing it correctly
cons.example: an owner deciding to shop independently once the compensation arrangement is stated

cons.claim: The boundary can feel absurd mid-conversation, because the operator must decline a question they may well know the answer to
cons.example: being asked which of two plans is cheaper for the client staff mix and having to route it

failure_modes: explaining how a plan works until it becomes a recommendation
accepting a fee arrangement without verifying the licensing class in the jurisdiction
disclosing verbally and only after the decision
remaining in the thread as a translator
treating a retirement-plan introduction like an ordinary product referral
acceptance_tests: every introduction into a licensed channel has a written compensation disclosure delivered before the introduction, a recorded client consent, and no operator-authored recommendation of a specific product, carrier or plan anywhere in the record
the applicable licensing class was verified before any compensation arrangement was accepted
revisit_triggers: a licensing, solicitation or disclosure rule change
a new compensation arrangement is offered to the operator
a client asks the operator to advise rather than to introduce
a receiving professional status or firm changes

base.update_signal: a change in licensing, solicitation or disclosure rules, or an introduction that drifted into advice

nodes.definition: An expansion offer inside a payroll relationship is made from an unusual position: the operator knows the client wages, their cash timing and their compliance exposure, the client depends on the operator for something they cannot easily move, and the offer frequently follows an event that frightened them. That combination makes ordinary sales technique unsafe, so the guardrail is explicit. Never sell from fear: an agency notice, a near-miss penalty or a discovered error is handled and closed first, and any offer arising from it is separated in time and framed by what the service does rather than by what might otherwise happen; describing exposure accurately when a client asks is legitimate, manufacturing dread is not. Disclose compensation before the recommendation rather than after the decision, for anything the operator earns on. Keep the base service unconditional, so nothing about payroll quality, priority or price depends on buying an add-on and a client can decline without any change in how they are treated, because an expansion that makes the base service feel contingent is coercion whatever the intent. Take particular care with clients who are overwhelmed, in distress, unfamiliar with the language of the offer, or dependent on the operator as their only professional adviser: a decision made by somebody who cannot evaluate it is not a sale, and the right move is usually to slow down, put the choice in writing and invite them to run it past their accountant. Finally, an offer the operator would not make to a sophisticated client is an offer that should not be made at all.

included: separation in time between incidents and offers
compensation disclosure before the recommendation
the unconditional base service rule
explicit care for overwhelmed, distressed or unadvised clients
the sophistication test
excluded: the acquisition-stage disclosure and penalty-talk rules used before a client signs
pricing and packaging design
declining to answer a client direct question about their exposure, which is the opposite failure

pros.claim: An offer that survives the guardrail leaves the relationship intact whether or not it is accepted
pros.example: a client who declines an add-on and stays for years because declining cost them nothing at all

pros.claim: The separation rule removes the operator own incentive distortion at the moment their judgement is worst
pros.example: not pitching a compliance service in the same call as an unresolved notice

cons.claim: The guardrail loses sales a more aggressive practice would close, and it will feel like leaving money on the table
cons.example: a competitor bundling an add-on immediately after a scare and winning the work

cons.claim: The line between accurately describing exposure and manufacturing fear is judgement, so a scrupulous operator can under-inform a client who needed to hear the risk
cons.example: softening a real multi-jurisdiction gap so much that the client does not act on it

failure_modes: pitching in the same conversation as an unresolved incident
disclosing compensation after the client has agreed
hinting that responsiveness follows the bundle
pressing a decision on an owner in visible distress
using a compliance scenario as a closing device
acceptance_tests: no expansion offer in the record is made in the same conversation as an unresolved incident or notice
every compensated offer has its disclosure timestamped before the recommendation, and declined offers show no subsequent change in service terms, priority or responsiveness
revisit_triggers: a client reports feeling pressured
an offer is found to have followed an incident too closely
a new compensated arrangement is added to the practice
a complaint or dispute touches how a service was sold

base.update_signal: a client account of feeling pressured, or an offer pattern that clusters after incidents

nodes.definition: Every recurring payroll relationship ends eventually, and the exit is the part of the service most visible to the people who will be asked about the operator later: the client accountant, the incoming provider and the partner who introduced them. Done properly it is a defined sequence. Agree the effective date against the calendar and prefer a quarter or year boundary, because a mid-year split creates a year-to-date and filing-responsibility seam that somebody will have to reconcile. Produce the departing client records in usable form, including registers, year-to-date figures, employee data, deduction and order details and the evidence file for filings made. State clearly which filings for the period fall to the platform under its agent role and which fall to the client and the incoming provider, since that ambiguity is the single most common source of a missed filing at a transition. Revoke standing access on both sides on the agreed date and dispose of retained personal data beyond what a records-retention obligation class requires, verified for the jurisdiction rather than assumed. Close the roster and residual records so the book and the statement stay true. The integrity part is simple and non-negotiable: the client data is the client, and delaying it, degrading it or pricing access to it as leverage is both wrong and the fastest way to convert one departure into a warning circulated among every referral source the operator has.

included: boundary-aligned effective date
complete record handover in usable form
the written filing-responsibility split
access revocation and data disposal by retention class
roster and residual closure
the no-leverage rule
excluded: performing the incoming provider setup or advising them
the client decision to leave, which is theirs
asserting retention periods or filing responsibilities, which are classes to verify
retention tactics aimed at reversing the decision

pros.claim: A clean and generous exit protects the referral network that produced the book in the first place
pros.example: a departing client accountant continuing to introduce new clients because the handover was faultless

pros.claim: An explicit filing-responsibility statement prevents the classic transition failure, a period nobody filed
pros.example: a mid-quarter departure where the split is written down and both providers know which return is theirs

cons.claim: A good exit is unpaid work on an account that is already gone
cons.example: assembling a complete evidence package for a client who cancelled with two weeks notice

cons.claim: Transparent handover occasionally exposes errors in the operator own history to a successor who will see them
cons.example: an incoming provider spotting a prior-period misconfiguration during the handover review

failure_modes: slow-walking the data export
splitting mid-quarter with no responsibility statement
leaving standing access live for months after departure
keeping personal data indefinitely
arguing about the decision instead of executing the exit
acceptance_tests: the departure has a recorded effective date with the filing-responsibility split stated in writing, a delivered record package acknowledged by the client, access revoked on both sides on that date, and retained personal data reduced to the documented retention class
revisit_triggers: the incoming provider or the client reports a gap after the transition
a retention obligation class changes
a departure has to land mid-quarter
a referral source raises the way an exit was handled

base.update_signal: a transition gap reported after an exit, which tightens the responsibility-split statement

edges.why_related: the charter names who performs which recurring act, which is what determines the minimum-necessary role each person actually needs
the routing reflex is the charter scope boundary applied to the questions that arrive between cycles
the obligation register is the charter duty list expressed as dated, evidenced items that roll
the preflight performs exactly the per-cycle acts the charter assigns to the service layer and stops at the acts it assigns to the client
the served roster used for the two-way match is the list of clients the charter is actually in force for
the variance review compares the finished run against the change log the preflight captured, so without an intake there is nothing to explain variances with
the funding path, method and cut-off checked at preflight are the same path whose settlement is then watched through to confirmation
the triage acts on what the variance review finds, and the window it can still use depends on how fast the review ran
the anomaly and its evidence are the raw material the router classifies into client, service-layer, platform or agency ownership
the quarter close is scheduled, owned and evidenced by the register, and its lead time is what makes reconciliation possible before the return
year-end starts from quarters that already reconcile, so unresolved quarterly variances become year-end problems with a more expensive correction class
the reset opens the year that year-end just closed, and the pay calendar and parameter work depends on the prior year being final
notice classification is meaningful only against a register that says what was owed, by whom and with what evidence
an escalation is only credible when the ownership classification and its evidence came first
the disclosure sequence starts the moment the router honestly classifies an issue as service-layer
how operator-caused defects are disclosed, contained and counted is what turns incidents into a defect trend rather than into departures
the defect trend is the first family of churn signals and it comes from the run-quality record
a silent drop on the statement is often the earliest hard evidence that a client relationship has already ended somewhere
expansion is only legitimate from a book whose runs are defect-free, and the same cycle evidence that measures quality is what surfaces need signals
the rung assessment is triggered by a dated need signal rather than by a growth target
the ladder identifies which rungs are introductions into licensed channels rather than service work, which is where the boundary applies
a recognised departure signal is what starts a planned exit rather than an improvised one
what the operator may observe and retain about a client bounds what evidence may be used to generate an offer, and data seen for service purposes is not a marketing asset
the production advice boundary sets the ceiling on what may be said in a benefits, retirement or insurance conversation before it becomes solicitation or advice
the peak-day and season model decides which rungs can be delivered at all, since a new recurring service lands on the same congested days
the guardrail governs when an observed need may become an offer, how it is framed and what must be disclosed before any recommendation
peak-day throughput pushes to shorten the pre-approval sequence exactly on the days when the most runs and the most risk are concentrated
edges.resolution_rule: preflight completeness wins without exception; capacity is fixed upstream by re-placing pay dates, standardising intake, hiring or declining work, and if a peak day genuinely cannot be served completely the run is rescheduled with the client rather than shortened

edges.why_related: the cheapest repair often needs a decision inside a closing window, but the decision is an employer determination the operator must not make
edges.resolution_rule: the operator stages every repair option but never chooses a determination reserved to the employer; when a window will close before the adviser answers, the operator states the deadline and its consequences in writing, the client decides, and where no decision arrives the default action taken is the reversible one

edges.why_related: expansion consumes exactly the attention and calendar days that defect-free delivery depends on, and the revenue case for growth is always more visible than the cost of a rising defect rate
edges.resolution_rule: run quality dominates growth: no additional recurring service and no additional client is taken on for a client or a book whose defect trend is rising or whose peak-day load already sits at the capacity model limit, until the trend is reversed or capacity is genuinely added

edges.why_related: retaining a struggling client pulls toward accommodating a funding request that would treat withheld employee tax as working capital
edges.resolution_rule: the withheld-funds boundary dominates every retention and revenue consideration: the operator presents lawful option classes, escalates to the client tax professional and counsel, documents the boundary in writing, and resigns the engagement rather than assisting if the client insists

edges.why_related: a rate, wage base or frequency that was never entered at the reset propagates silently into every deposit and first becomes visible as a first-quarter reconciliation variance
repeated funding stress both predicts departure and precipitates it, because platform funding restrictions change the client experience of the whole arrangement
how long a platform-owned defect stays open is what the client actually experiences as service quality, regardless of who caused it
ownership and its evidence are established before a repair path is chosen, because who caused it changes who decides, who pays and which evidence the repair will need
revocation and data disposal are performed on the agreed exit date and only after the record package has been delivered and acknowledged, never before
whatever the quarterly reconciliation discovers becomes a new intake question or trigger in the per-cycle sequence so the same class is caught in-cycle next time
notice outcomes rewrite the register, adding a rate, a changed frequency, a new account or an obligation class nobody had listed
both are pre-commitment sweeps performed against a deadline after which the same error changes class and cost, and both fail the same way when they are started too late

conflict_axes.name: run_day_speed_versus_preflight_completeness
conflict_axes.description: Every cycle sets the pressure to approve and move on against the sequence that keeps the run defect-free, and the pressure is worst on the days when several clients pay at once.
poles: approve on time whatever is outstanding
complete every pre-approval check first
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat completeness as fixed and treat the schedule as the variable: re-place pay dates, chase intake earlier, or move the run with the client rather than skipping a check

conflict_axes.name: repair_speed_versus_determination_ownership
conflict_axes.description: Correction windows close on a clock the operator can see and the client often cannot, while the decisions inside those windows belong to the employer and sometimes to their adviser.
poles: act now inside the window
wait for the party who owns the decision
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stage every option, state the window and its consequence in writing immediately, let the client decide, and where nothing arrives take only the reversible action

conflict_axes.name: platform_ownership_versus_client_experience_ownership
conflict_axes.description: Many defects genuinely belong to the platform, and yet the client experiences them as the operator service failing, so technical correctness and relationship reality point in different directions.
poles: it is the platform issue to resolve
the client experience is the operator responsibility
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route the defect honestly by evidence while owning the client-facing plan, the workaround and the status, and never hand the client the operator frustration with the vendor

conflict_axes.name: growth_versus_run_quality
conflict_axes.description: New clients and new recurring services compete for exactly the calendar days and attention that defect-free delivery consumes, and the revenue is visible immediately while the quality cost appears a quarter later.
poles: take the growth now
protect the delivery standard
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate every addition on the defect trend and the peak-day model, and add capacity or standardise before adding load

conflict_axes.name: helpfulness_versus_the_advice_boundary
conflict_axes.description: The most useful-seeming answer is frequently the one the operator is not the licensed provider of, and refusing it can look like evasion to a client who trusts them.
poles: answer the question the client actually asked
route it to the party who may answer it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer mechanical questions fully and generously, route determination and professional-class questions with the question written down for the adviser, and never let the refusal be the whole response

conflict_axes.name: retention_effort_versus_the_client_right_to_leave
conflict_axes.description: Switching costs make a departing payroll client easy to obstruct, which is precisely why the temptation to slow an exit exists at all.
poles: work to keep every account
accept the decision and exit cleanly
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: respond to signals with causes and honest conversation before the switching window, and once the decision is made switch entirely to a fast, complete, no-leverage exit

conflict_axes.name: self_disclosure_versus_short_term_account_risk
conflict_axes.description: Disclosing an operator-caused error early invites consequences that silence might have avoided, while silence converts a recoverable incident into a breach of trust when the client finds out elsewhere.
poles: wait until the fix is known
disclose before the client discovers it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclose first with what is known and what is in motion, contain the recurrence, then remedy, and never promise an outcome that belongs to an agency

conflict_axes.name: year_end_capture_versus_new_year_readiness
conflict_axes.description: The same few weeks carry two irreversible deadlines, one for items that must land inside the closing year and one for parameters that must be right before the first run of the next.
poles: finish the closing year first
get the new year parameters in place first
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sequence by irreversibility: in-year items that cannot be fixed after the final run come first, except rate and frequency notices that would misstate the first deposits of the new year, which are entered as they arrive

conflict_axes.name: client_convenience_versus_data_protection_friction
conflict_axes.description: Every verification step and every narrow role is friction experienced by a client or a colleague who is in a hurry, and the fraud it prevents is invisible when it works.
poles: make the change quickly as asked
verify out of band and keep access minimal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep verification non-negotiable for anything that moves money or changes identity, and buy back the speed elsewhere with prepared channels, standing contacts and a second trained approver

conflict_axes.name: client_cash_pressure_versus_the_withheld_funds_boundary
conflict_axes.description: A client short of cash on a pay date will look for flexibility in the one place that appears to offer it, the tax portion of the run, and the operator is the person they ask.
poles: help the client through the squeeze
hold the line on withheld funds
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: present only lawful option classes, escalate to the client tax professional and counsel, document the boundary in writing, and resign rather than assist if the client insists

edge_cases.description: A client with owner-only payroll drops to no wages for several months while the entity and its tax accounts stay open, and everybody assumes nothing is due
edge_cases.trigger: headcount and wages fall to zero without the accounts being closed
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the obligation register live because zero-wage periods generally carry their own reporting classes, confirm with the client adviser whether accounts should be closed or kept dormant, and treat the drop as a churn signal at the same time

edge_cases.description: An email that looks exactly like a current employee asks to change their direct-deposit account the day before the run
edge_cases.trigger: a banking change request arrives through an unverified channel under time pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: verify out of band against a contact detail held before the request, never using the contact information supplied in the request, and hold the change to the following run rather than compressing the verification

edge_cases.description: A remote employee moved to another state mid-quarter and nobody mentioned it until the quarterly reconciliation showed a jurisdiction that had never been registered
edge_cases.trigger: an employee relocation reaches the operator only through reconciliation evidence
edge_cases.mitigation: write the fact into the register immediately, open the registration obligation class for the jurisdiction, place the correction on the window ladder, and route the classification and amendment decisions to the client and their tax professional

edge_cases.description: The platform shows a filing as submitted while the agency sends a notice saying nothing was received for the period
edge_cases.trigger: platform status and agency records disagree about a filing the platform performed
edge_cases.mitigation: pull the filing confirmation evidence rather than the dashboard status, open a platform case with the notice and the confirmation attached and the notice deadline stated, and route the response itself to the client tax professional

edge_cases.description: The payroll debit fails for a long-standing client who has never missed one, on the morning of the pay date
edge_cases.trigger: a funding failure with no prior warning signal
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm the cause with the client and the platform in the same hour, present the option classes that exist within the platform rules and the jurisdiction pay-timing classes, state the withheld-funds boundary, and record the whole exchange

edge_cases.description: An employee tells the client about a shortfall in their pay before the operator has finished diagnosing an error the operator caused
edge_cases.trigger: an operator-caused defect is discovered by an affected employee first
edge_cases.mitigation: disclose immediately with what is known and what is in motion rather than waiting for a complete answer, contain the recurrence before repairing the instance, and sweep the book for the same defect the same day

edge_cases.description: A bonus paid by cheque outside the payroll system in November surfaces during the year-end sweep after the final scheduled run has already gone
edge_cases.trigger: an in-year item is disclosed after the last run of the year
edge_cases.mitigation: place the item on the window ladder immediately, present the remaining repair classes including an additional run before the year cut-off if one is still possible, and route the taxability and valuation questions to the client accountant

edge_cases.description: A newly appointed accountant tells the client to move payroll to a different platform mid-year
edge_cases.trigger: a new adviser arrives with their own preferred stack
edge_cases.mitigation: have the straight conversation early with the run-quality record rather than a discount, and if the decision holds, plan the exit onto a quarter boundary with a written filing-responsibility split

edge_cases.description: A client who is plainly still being served disappears from the partner residual statement with no notification
edge_cases.trigger: a silent drop between the served roster and the statement
edge_cases.mitigation: open a dated case with the partner contact immediately rather than waiting for the next period, re-verify the current crediting rules and any account change on the client side, and keep serving the client while it is resolved

edge_cases.description: An owner asks the operator to run payroll now and hold back the tax portion for two weeks because a large customer paid late
edge_cases.trigger: a client proposes using withheld employee tax as short-term working capital
edge_cases.mitigation: state the boundary plainly and in writing, present only lawful option classes, escalate to the client tax professional and counsel the same day, and resign the engagement rather than participate if the client proceeds

edge_cases.description: A client asks the operator to take over their bookkeeping starting next month, in the week the book is already at its peak season load
edge_cases.trigger: an expansion request arrives during a capacity peak
edge_cases.mitigation: run the rung assessment against the peak-day and season model before agreeing anything, propose a start date outside the season or refer the work out, and never accept a start date that lands the first close inside quarter-end payroll work

edge_cases.description: A benefits broker offers the operator a fee for introducing payroll clients who need coverage
edge_cases.trigger: a compensated referral arrangement is proposed in a licensed field
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the licensing and compensation obligation classes in the jurisdiction before accepting anything, disclose the arrangement in writing before any introduction, record client consent, and keep every product question with the licensed professional

workflow.action: Convert the signed onboarding handoff into a standing service charter
workflow.description: Restate the arrangement as a repeating cycle: the per-cycle acts of each party, the covered-versus-billable line, the response classes and the interval at which the register is re-read
workflow.artifact: standing service and duty register with a dated last review
workflow.gate: every recurring obligation resolves to one named owner with a cadence, a lead time and an evidence type, and the billable classes are named in writing

workflow.action: Reduce standing access to minimum necessary and install out-of-band verification
workflow.description: Map every operator-side account to a person and a narrow role, set the review interval and the revocation rule, and define the channel for sensitive documents and money-moving changes
workflow.gate: no shared or over-broad accounts remain, and a verification path using pre-held contact details exists for every banking or identity change

workflow.action: Install the question-routing reflex and its written trail
workflow.description: Define the mechanical, determination-class and professional-class buckets, the referral sentence, the adviser contacts and where the record of each routed question lives
workflow.artifact: question routing rule with adviser contact list
workflow.gate: the three buckets are written with examples, and a record location is named for referrals and for client determinations

workflow.action: Stand the compliance calendar up as a live rolling register
workflow.description: Give every obligation class an owner, a cadence, a lead time and an evidence type, define the rolling closure and the fact-change write-in rule, and set how platform-performed filings are verified
workflow.artifact: rolling obligation register with evidence slots
workflow.gate: every open item has an owner, a next-due date, a lead time and an evidence type, and each platform-performed filing has a named verification method

workflow.action: Build the per-cycle preflight and the archived run record
workflow.description: Write the change-log intake, the mechanical preconditions, the register-reading step and the named-approver act, then run a full cycle against them
workflow.gate: a complete cycle produces an archived approved preview with its change log, the approver identity and the approval timestamp

workflow.action: Add the post-run variance trigger list and the funding watch
workflow.description: Define the anomaly triggers compared against the prior run and the funding path, cut-off and settlement confirmation for each client
workflow.artifact: variance trigger list and per-client funding path record
workflow.gate: a run is reviewed against the trigger list inside the correction window and its settlement is confirmed rather than assumed

workflow.action: Define the correction window ladder before the first incident needs it
workflow.description: Write the repair classes from preview through prior-year, which windows each depends on, who decides at each step and what the operator must never decide
workflow.artifact: correction window ladder and triage template
workflow.gate: each window class names its deadline source, its repair options with impacts, and the determinations reserved to the client and their adviser

workflow.action: Rehearse issue routing, platform escalation and the own-error sequence
workflow.description: Write the four-way ownership classification with its evidence rule, the case package standard for the partner channel, and the disclose, contain, remedy, record sequence with its promise boundary
workflow.artifact: issue routing rule, case package standard and incident sequence
workflow.gate: the case package standard requires reproduction, expected against actual, a deadline with a consequence and an owner, and the incident sequence states the promise boundary and the book-wide sweep

workflow.action: Run quarter close against the register lead times
workflow.description: Reconcile wages and each tax by jurisdiction to deposits, check mid-quarter jurisdiction and zero-wage cases, capture fringe timing and trace in-quarter corrections through
workflow.gate: wages and each tax agree to deposits with every variance corrected before the return or listed with its disposition and routed to the client tax professional

workflow.action: Execute the year-end sweep and then the new-year parameter reset
workflow.description: Ask the annual item classes early enough to process them in-year, verify identity data, reconcile the final run, then reset the annual parameter classes and build the new pay calendar
workflow.artifact: year-end sweep record and new-year parameter sheet
workflow.gate: every sweep item class has a recorded client answer before the final run, and every parameter class carries a current-year value or an explicit not-applicable before the first run of the new year

workflow.action: Measure run quality, reconcile the residual statement and re-fit capacity
workflow.description: Record defects per run by class and origin, match the statement two ways against the served roster, and rebuild the peak-day and season capacity model from recorded time
workflow.artifact: defect trend, reconciled statement and capacity model
workflow.gate: every run has a defect record including zeros, every statement difference is explained or opened as a dated case, and the capacity model states peak-day and season loads with a reserve

workflow.action: Open expansion only through logged need signals inside the guardrail
workflow.description: Log need signals with evidence and date, assess any rung for load and obligation class before offering it, and apply the disclosure, separation and unconditional-service rules to every offer
workflow.artifact: need-signal log with dispositions and rung assessments
workflow.gate: every offer traces to a dated signal with evidence and a completed rung assessment, carries its compensation disclosure before the recommendation, and sits outside any conversation about an unresolved incident

dominance_rules.rule: Compliance-critical accuracy dominates client convenience and operator throughput
dominance_rules.rationale: payroll errors carry penalty, interest and employee-trust consequences that no amount of speed recovers
dominance_rules.trigger: a choice arises between completing a check and meeting a convenience or schedule expectation
dominance_rules.action: complete the check and move the schedule, the placement or the workload instead

dominance_rules.rationale: an operator who is not the licensed provider creates exposure for the client and for themselves the moment a casual answer is relied on
dominance_rules.trigger: a determination-class or professional-class question arrives, especially informally on run day
dominance_rules.action: route it with the question written down for the adviser, record the client own determination, and never supply the conclusion

dominance_rules.rule: The withheld-funds boundary dominates retention and revenue
dominance_rules.rationale: withheld employee tax is not the client money and assisting its use as working capital converts a service into participation in a serious problem
dominance_rules.trigger: a client proposes delaying, reducing or borrowing against the tax portion of a run
dominance_rules.action: present lawful option classes, escalate to the client tax professional and counsel, document the boundary, and resign rather than assist if the client insists

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure dominates self-protection when the error belongs to the operator
dominance_rules.rationale: concealment is the failure clients do not forgive, and it compounds while the same defect keeps running
dominance_rules.trigger: an issue is classified as service-layer
dominance_rules.action: disclose before the client discovers it, contain the recurrence, then remedy, and promise nothing that belongs to an agency

dominance_rules.rule: Data minimisation and verification dominate convenience in access and money-moving changes
dominance_rules.rationale: the book concentrates identifiers and banking details that are a standing fraud target, and one incident is unrecoverable
dominance_rules.trigger: any request for broader access, a faster channel, or a banking or identity change
dominance_rules.action: keep the narrowest role, use the auditable channel, and verify out of band against a contact detail held before the request

dominance_rules.rationale: repair cost rises in steps as money and filings travel, so hesitation converts an adjustment into an amendment
dominance_rules.trigger: an error is found while a cancellation, same-period or in-year window is still open
dominance_rules.action: state the deadline and its consequence in writing immediately and stage the reversible option while the client decides

dominance_rules.rationale: the defect trend is the leading indicator of churn, and growth bought with quality destroys the book that funds it
dominance_rules.trigger: a new client or a new recurring service would land on a peak day or on a rising defect trend
dominance_rules.action: decline, defer or re-place the work until the capacity model and the trend genuinely support it

dominance_rules.rationale: an operator whose only hold is the difficulty of leaving has already lost the account and poisons the referral network on the way out
dominance_rules.trigger: a client signals departure or declines an offer
dominance_rules.action: respond with causes, honest conversation and a clean exit path, never with friction, leverage or a change in service quality

dominance_rules.rule: Verified current terms dominate remembered ones
dominance_rules.rationale: partner-program terms, platform inclusions, licensing rules and filing obligations all change without notice and are jurisdiction-specific
dominance_rules.trigger: any statement about compensation, platform coverage, licensing or a filing obligation is about to be relied on or told to a client
dominance_rules.action: verify against the current program document, the current platform documentation or the current rule in the operating jurisdiction before acting

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the standing duty register before the first production cycle rather than after the first missed obligation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing who owned what in the middle of an incident, with a deadline already running

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write every client fact change into the obligation register the week it happens
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a whole quarter of deposits and reporting computed against an obligation set that no longer matches the business

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the preview register against the change log before approval instead of reading totals afterwards
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reversals, off-cycle runs, amended returns and employee conversations that all begin after money has moved

anti_rework_rules.rule: Classify issue ownership with evidence before escalating to anyone
anti_rework_rules.prevents: days lost in the wrong queue and the loss of credibility that makes the next genuine escalation slower

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ask the year-end sweep questions before the final scheduled run of the year
anti_rework_rules.prevents: corrected wage statements, employee re-issues and a client exposed in front of their own staff

anti_rework_rules.rule: Enter agency rate and frequency notices before the first run of the new year
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a full year of deposits computed on last year parameters and discovered at a quarter close

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a platform-performed filing by its confirmation rather than by its dashboard status
anti_rework_rules.prevents: learning about a non-filing from an agency notice once penalty and interest classes are already accruing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Assess a new service rung for calendar load and obligation class before offering it to anyone
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a new line of business colliding with quarter close and degrading the payroll book that funds it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile the residual statement against the served roster every period
anti_rework_rules.prevents: chasing a dropped or mis-credited client after the partner own inquiry window has closed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Close the configuration defect before repairing the instance it produced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the same error running again during the cleanup and turning one incident into a lost account

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect reaches settlement or a filing
iteration_protocol.action: add the missing check to the preflight or the variance trigger list, sweep the book for the same defect class, and record the control change

iteration_protocol.trigger: quarter close finds a variance the in-cycle checks should have caught
iteration_protocol.action: move the check earlier in the cycle, re-verify the affected periods and update the register evidence requirement

iteration_protocol.trigger: an agency notice arrives for an obligation that is not on the register
iteration_protocol.action: add the obligation class with its owner, cadence, lead time and evidence, then sweep the book for clients with the same fact pattern

iteration_protocol.trigger: a platform case stalls past its next-check date or a resolution fails verification in live data
iteration_protocol.action: escalate a step in the partner channel, re-open with the failed verification attached, and keep the workaround and the client status running

iteration_protocol.trigger: the defect trend rises for a client or for a defect class across consecutive cycles
iteration_protocol.action: pause expansion for that client, diagnose the origin class, and re-fit the capacity model before accepting new work

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client leaves without any churn signal having triggered
iteration_protocol.action: add the missed signal to the watch list and review the exit for what the recurring service could have seen and did not

iteration_protocol.trigger: a residual statement difference that no known mechanism explains, or a partner-program term change
iteration_protocol.action: open a dated case with the partner contact, re-derive the movement mechanisms and re-verify the current terms and crediting rules

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client reports feeling pressured, or an offer is found to have followed an incident too closely
iteration_protocol.action: withdraw the offer, re-time it under the separation rule, and re-check the disclosure record for the whole period

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new jurisdiction, benefit, entity, withholding order or platform module appears at a client
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the duty register, write the fact into the obligation calendar the same week, and re-place the client against the capacity model

priority_rationale: The charter, the access discipline and the advice boundary come first because every later act inherits from them: what the recurring service owes each cycle, who owns each obligation, how the most sensitive data a small employer holds may be touched, and which questions leave the operator entirely. The obligation register follows, because it is the mechanism that converts those duties into dated, evidenced, rolling items. The per-cycle units come next in their natural order, preflight before variance review before correction triage, because each one exists to catch an error while the previous stage repair class is still available and cheap. The calendar seasons build on the cycle: quarter close reconciles what the runs produced, year-end depends on quarters that already reconcile, and the new-year reset opens the book the year-end just closed. Triage sits after the cycle because ownership can only be classified against evidence the cycle produced, and the own-error sequence is what converts a defect into a control change rather than into a departure. Retention, churn watch, residual reconciliation and capacity then compose the whole book into something measurable. Expansion comes last on purpose: it is legitimate only from a book whose runs are defect-free, whose capacity is modelled and whose offers are governed by disclosure, licensing and the guardrail, and the exit unit closes the loop by making departure as clean as arrival.
